title: 2020 HMMT Invitational Problem 3
statement: Let \(P_{1} P_{2} P_{3} P_{4}\) be a tetrahedron in \(\mathbb{R}^{3}\) and let \(O\) be a point equidistant from each of its vertices. Suppose there exists a point \(H\) such that for each \(i\), the line \(P_{i} H\) is perpendicular to the plane through the other three vertices. Line \(P_{1} H\) intersects the plane through \(P_{2}, P_{3}, P_{4}\) at \(A\), and contains a point \(B \neq P_{1}\) such that \(O P_{1}=O B\). Show that \(H B=3 H A\).

solutions.text:
We use vectors with \(H\) as the origin. Then \(P_{i} \cdot\left(P_{j}-P_{k}\right)=0\) from the definition of \(H\). Thus \(P_{i} \cdot P_{j}=P_{i} \cdot P_{k}\) for any distinct \(i, j, k\). In particular, the quantity \(P_{i} \cdot P_{j}\) is a constant over all distinct choices of \(i, j\). Let this value be \(D\). Let

\[O^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2}\left(P_{1}+P_{2}+P_{3}+P_{4}\right)\]

We claim \(O^{\prime}=O\). To see this, note that

\[\left(O^{\prime}-P_{1}\right) \cdot\left(O^{\prime}-P_{1}\right)=\frac{1}{4}\left(P_{2}+P_{3}+P_{4}-P_{1}\right) \cdot\left(P_{2}+P_{3}+P_{4}-P_{1}\right)\]

will be symmetric after expanding. Thus \(O^{\prime}\) is equidistant from the \(P_{i}\) 's, which means \(O^{\prime}=O\).
Now, the projection of \(O\) onto \(P_{1} H\) is \(\frac{O \cdot P_{1}}{P_{1} \cdot P_{1}} P_{1}\), so

\[B=P_{1}\left(\frac{\left(2 O-P_{1}\right) \cdot P_{1}}{P_{1} \cdot P_{1}}\right)=P_{1}\left(\frac{3 D}{P_{1} \cdot P_{1}}\right)\]

Meanwhile, \(A\) is the projection of \(P_{2}\) on \(P_{1} H\), so

\[A=P_{1}\left(\frac{P_{1} \cdot P_{2}}{P_{1} \cdot P_{1}}\right)=P_{1}\left(\frac{D}{P_{1} \cdot P_{1}}\right)\]

Thus \(H B=3 H A\), as desired.
